Commentary.Commentary: Back with the chase! The English players are out in the field, taking their respective positions. Also, out walk the openers of India Women, where Smriti Mandhana will open the innings alongside Pratika Rawal. Kate Cross has the new ball in her hands, and she will start the proceedings with one slip in place. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

On a wicket that looks good to bat on, England Women will be on the hunt for early wickets, while for India Women, a solid start will be key. How the Indian batting unit handles England’s spin threat in the middle overs could well decide the outcome. Join us in a bit for the second innings!

The final five overs belonged to England Women, as Dunkley launched a late assault to lift the scoring rate and Ecclestone provided excellent support at the other end, as the duo added 55 runs, finishing strongly and pushing England to 258. From India’s perspective, the bowling was steady and spinners were the standout but lacked the finishing sting in the death overs. Sneh Rana was the standout, keeping things tight and grabbing two crucial wickets, and Kranti Goud also chipped in with two wickets upfront. Shree Charani and Amanjot Kaur picked up one wicket each.

Things got even worse for the home side as Sneh struck in quick succession to remove the two set batters. Spinners continued to build on pressure and didn't give away any looseners to score runs. But the pair of Dunkley and Davidson-Richards hung in there to keep ticking the scoreboard with singles and doubles. Kranti dropped Richards when she was on 16 and in the next over, Dunkley also got a reprieve on 22. The pair continued to build on their partnership with both Dunkley and Alice bringing up their half centuries.

Earlier, England Women won the toss and elected to bat first, but the openers departed early inside the first 4 overs. After that, Natalie Sciver-Brunt and Emma Lamb formed a good partnership to steady the ship as England were 55/2 at the end of the Powerplay. However, once the field got spread out and spinners came into the attack, India kept things tight and didn't give any loose balls to put away for a boundary. At one point, there were no boundaries for 35 balls, which resulted in a breakthrough as Sneh Rana broke the partnership between Emma and Natalie.

36 runs off the last 3 overs and 76 runs in the last 10 overs for England and they will be pleased with what they have on the board. It was largely thanks to the brilliant partnership between Sophia Dunkley and Alice Davidson-Richards. After early blows had them at 20/2, the middle order steadied the innings before India choked the scoring in the middle overs, where England struggled to find boundaries. Just when it looked like England might fall short, Dunkley’s fluent 83 and Davidson-Richards’ composed 53 revived the momentum. A late flourish, with 49 runs coming in the last five overs, helped push the score to a respectable mark. With spinners getting turn, this target could test India if England bowl with discipline.

Following a historic T20I series victory, a confident India Women's team will look to carry their momentum into the three-match ODI series against England, starting with the first match in Southampton. The 'Women in Blue' secured their first-ever T20I series win on English soil by a 3-2 margin, and now, with the ODI World Cup on home soil later this year, this series is a crucial final tune-up. For India, the T20I series showcased their formidable batting depth and a rejuvenated fielding unit. Skipper Harmanpreet Kaur, along with the explosive Smriti Mandhana and finisher Richa Ghosh, provides a powerful batting order. The addition of players like Jemimah Rodrigues, Harleen Deol, and rising star Pratika Rawal, who has been in record-breaking form, gives India the firepower to post big totals, a stated goal of the team. However, their bowling attack faces a significant test. With frontline pacers Titas Sadhu, Renuka Singh, and Pooja Vastrakar all ruled out due to injuries, the pace attack will be led by Arundhati Reddy, with support from all-rounders. The spin department will be key, with the experienced duo of Deepti Sharma and Radha Yadav, along with the promising left-arm spinner Shree Charani, tasked with controlling the middle overs and taking wickets. England, on the other hand, will be eager to bounce back after their T20I series defeat. They are bolstered by the return of key players who missed parts of the T20I series. Captain Natalie Sciver-Brunt, one of the world's most versatile all-rounders, is back to lead the side after a groin issue. The home side also welcomes back Sophie Ecclestone, the world's number one ODI bowler, who returns to the ODI setup. Their presence will significantly strengthen England's bowling and batting lineups. With a powerful batting lineup featuring the likes of Tammy Beaumont, Amy Jones, and Sophia Dunkley, England will be looking to reassert their dominance on home soil. The Utilita Bowl in Southampton is expected to offer a batting-friendly, flat surface with consistent bounce, ideal for stroke play. While pacers may get some early swing under partly cloudy skies, spinners are likely to find grip in the middle overs.  In ODIs, England holds a slight edge over India, with a head-to-head record of 40-34 in their favor. However, India's recent form and confidence from the T20I series victory make them a strong contender to challenge England's historical dominance in the 50-over format. This series promises to be an exciting contest between two of the world's best women's cricket teams.
